data.summary: This 16‑week plan uses the student’s 3‑hour weekly block to cover all AP Physics 1 units, beginning with the weak units (6 and 7) and revisiting them before the exam. Each week focuses on a specific set of topics, provides concrete tasks that can be completed in one sitting, and reserves the last two weeks for mixed review and timed practice.

weeks.focus: Start with Energy and Momentum of Rotating Systems – build a strong foundation in rotational kinetic energy.
tasks: Read the textbook section on rotational kinetic energy and write a summary of the formula.

weeks.focus: Continue unit 6, covering torque and work.
tasks: Solve 5 torque‑work problems from the AP practice set and check solutions.

weeks.focus: Complete unit 6 with angular momentum concepts.
tasks: Create flashcards for angular momentum conservation and quiz yourself.

weeks.focus: Begin unit 7, defining simple harmonic motion.
tasks: Draw the displacement‑time graph for a mass‑spring system and label key points.
Calculate the period of a pendulum with given length and compare to the formula.
Plot velocity vs. time for SHM and identify amplitude and phase shift.
Derive the total energy expression for a mass‑spring system and verify with numerical example.

weeks.focus: Unit 1 Kinematics – Scalars and Vectors in One Dimension.
tasks: Convert 10 m/s to km/h and vice versa; solve 3 related word problems.
Compute average velocity and acceleration for a given motion graph.
Sketch position‑time and velocity‑time graphs for a car accelerating then decelerating.

weeks.focus: Vectors and motion in two dimensions.
tasks: Resolve a 45° launch into horizontal and vertical components and calculate range.

weeks.focus: Force and translational dynamics – Newton’s laws.
tasks: Draw free‑body diagrams for 3 scenarios and solve for unknown forces.

weeks.focus: Work, energy, and power – translational kinetic energy.
tasks: Compute work done by a force over a distance and verify energy conservation in a roller‑coaster segment.
Simulate an elastic collision with given masses and velocities; calculate final speeds.

weeks.focus: Mixed review – rotational dynamics and fluids.
tasks: Solve 2 problems each from torque, rotational inertia, and fluid pressure; compare answers.
Take a full 60‑minute timed AP practice quiz; review mistakes and create a summary of key formulas.

data.final_week_advice: In the final week, focus on pacing, reviewing mistakes, and reinforcing confidence with timed practice. Ensure you’re comfortable with all formulae and problem‑solving steps before the exam.
